# Quilldown: full text

> The complete text of Quilldown's product pages and guides in one file, for language models and other automated readers. Canonical addresses are given under each title.

---

Features

# Everything Quilldown does, explained plainly

Quilldown is a free online Markdown editor that runs in your browser. Here's a complete look at what it can do, from live preview and tables to math, diagrams and export, along with the few things it can't.

[Open the editor](https://quilldown.vercel.app/#editor)
[Read the docs](https://quilldown.vercel.app/docs)

Writing and live preview

## Write on one side, see the result on the other

### Live preview

Every heading, list, table and code block renders as you type. You see the finished page while you write, so mistakes show up straight away instead of after you export.

Markdown on the left, the finished page on the right

```
# Launch notes

Ship **fast**, write _well_.

- [ ] Draft the announcement
- [ ] Review with the team

| Plan   | Price |
| ------ | ----- |
| Editor | Free  |

`npm run build`
```

Launch notes

Ship fast, write well.

-   Draft the announcement

-   Review with the team

Plan |
Price |

Editor |
Free |

npm run build

### Scroll that stays in sync

Scroll the editor and the preview follows, and the other way around. Quilldown lines the two panes up block by block, so a long table or code block doesn't throw them out of step.

### Code that's easy to read

Fenced code blocks are syntax-highlighted for dozens of languages. Each block has a one-click copy button in the preview.

### GitHub Flavored Markdown

You get everything in standard Markdown plus tables, task lists, strikethrough, autolinks and fenced code. It's the same flavor GitHub, GitLab and most documentation tools use, so what you write here behaves the same there.

### Choose your layout

Use split view, editor only or preview only, and drag the divider to change the balance. On a phone the editor shows one pane at a time, and you switch between writing and preview from the top bar.

Formatting tools

## Tools that keep your hands on the keyboard

### 45+ one-click snippets

One toolbar covers text styles, headings, lists, tables, math, diagrams and callouts. If you'd rather not memorize syntax, click. If you know it, just type.

Bold and italicHeadingsListsTask listsLinks and imagesTablesCode blocksMathDiagramsCallouts

### Keyboard shortcuts

Hover any toolbar button to see its shortcut. On a Mac, use ⌘ instead of Ctrl. Press Enter to continue a list and Tab to indent it.

- BoldCtrlB

- ItalicCtrlI

- LinkCtrlK

- Inline codeCtrlE

- FindCtrlF

- ReplaceCtrlH

- OpenCtrlO

- SaveCtrlS

### Find and replace

Matches are highlighted as you type. You can match case, match whole words or use regular expressions, then replace one match or all of them. "Replace all" counts as a single undo step, so you can reverse it in one go.

### Outline sidebar

All your headings appear in a clickable list that follows your scroll position. In a long document, you can jump to any section in one click.

### Callouts

Add Note, Tip, Important, Warning and Caution boxes in GitHub's style from a single dropdown.

### Emoji picker and shortcodes

Search by name, browse categories, pick a skin tone and return to your recent choices. You can also type a colon and a few letters, like :roc, and pick from the suggestions. A finished :tada: turns into 🎉.

Math, diagrams and tables

## More than plain text

### LaTeX math

Write inline math between single dollar signs and display math between double dollar signs. It renders with KaTeX, including fractions, sums, integrals, matrices and aligned equations. Useful for lecture notes, problem sets and technical writing.

Inline and display math

```
Euler's identity, $e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0$, links five constants.

$$
x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}
$$
```

Euler's identity, eiπ+1=0e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0eiπ+1=0, links five constants.

x=−b±b2−4ac2ax = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}x=2a−b±b2−4ac​​

### Mermaid diagrams

Draw diagrams from plain text: flowcharts, sequence diagrams, class diagrams, state diagrams, ER diagrams, Gantt charts, pie charts and mind maps. Each type has a ready-made template to start from, and diagrams follow your light or dark theme.

mermaid · Flowchart

```
flowchart LR
A[Write Markdown] --> B{Looks right?}
B -- Yes --> C[Export or share]
B -- No --> A
```

### A visual table editor

Building tables by typing pipes is tedious. Instead, edit in a grid: add rows and columns, set alignment for each column and paste rows straight from Excel or Google Sheets. You get tidy, aligned Markdown back.

| Plan | Price |

| :--- | ---: |

| Editor | Free |

| Exports | Free |

Plan | Price |

Editor | Free |

Exports | Free |

### Footnotes

Write [^1] where a note belongs and Quilldown numbers it, collects the notes at the bottom and links both ways. In a Word export they become real footnotes.

### Images

Paste a screenshot or drop a picture into the editor. It's resized, stored inside the document and embedded when you export. Since images are stored in your browser along with the document, a document with many large images can reach the browser's storage limit sooner than a text-only one.

### Templates

Start from a README, meeting notes, résumé, blog post, email, tables, to-do list or general notes. Each template opens in its own tab.

Documents and files

## Keep several documents open, and never lose your place

### Tabs

Open multiple documents like browser tabs. Drag to reorder, double-click to rename and middle-click to close. If you close a tab by accident, the Undo button in the message that appears brings it back.

notes.mdreadme.mddraft.md+

### Open and drop files

Open .md, .markdown or .txt files from your computer, or drag several onto the page at once. Each one lands in its own tab.

### Save back to the original file

In Chrome and Edge, a tab can stay linked to a file on your computer. A small dot shows the link, and an orange dot means you have unsaved changes. Ctrl+S then saves straight back to the file. In other browsers, Ctrl+S downloads a .md file instead.

### Autosave

Every tab is saved in your browser as you type, so your draft is there when you return.

### Open with Quilldown

Once you've installed Quilldown as an app, it can appear in your system's "Open with" menu for .md files.

Copy and export

## Send your writing wherever it needs to go

You choose the format at the end. Everything is created in your browser, so nothing is uploaded to produce a file.

### Copy it four ways

From either pane you can copy formatted text, Markdown, clean HTML, or a version made for pasting into Google Docs. That last one uses heading sizes Docs understands (23 pt for H1, 17 pt for H2, 14 pt for H3 and 12 pt for body text) and sets no font, so the text takes on your document's own font.

Formatted textCopy for DocsMarkdownHTML

### Seven export formats

Pick a format, and Quilldown builds the file on your device.

Format |
Best for |
One thing to know |

PDF |
Print-ready files. Best for equations, since they render exactly as they do in the preview. |
Made through your browser's print dialog by choosing "Save as PDF". If code blocks or tables look flat, turn on "Background graphics" in the print options. |

Word (.docx) |
A real Word document that also opens in Google Docs and Pages. |
Equations stay as their TeX source text and diagrams are inserted as images. |

PNG |
An image of the whole document. |
Very long documents are too tall for one image, so use PDF for those. |

EPUB |
An e-book for Apple Books, Kobo and other readers. |
Nothing to watch for. |

HTML |
A standalone, styled web page you can host or send. |
Nothing to watch for. |

Markdown (.md) |
Your plain source file. |
Nothing to watch for. |

Plain text (.txt) |
The same content with no markup. |
The formatting is dropped, by design. |

### Exports are always light

Even if you write in dark mode, exports come out in a clean, print-friendly light style.

### Generated in your browser

Copying and every export happen on your device. Nothing is sent to a server. [Read the privacy details](https://quilldown.vercel.app/privacy).

Privacy and offline

## Private by design, useful without a connection

### Nothing is uploaded

Quilldown runs entirely in your browser. What you write is never sent to a server, and there's no account, so there's no cloud copy either. Your drafts are saved on your own device.

### No third-party requests while you write

Every library, font and icon ships with the site. You can check this yourself in your browser's network panel.

### Works offline

After your first visit, a service worker caches the site, so Quilldown loads and exports without a connection.

### Install it as an app

In Chrome, Edge and other browsers that support it, an Install button lets you run Quilldown like a desktop or phone app.

### Open source

The code is public on [GitHub](https://github.com/Dhruv-Dhameliya/quilldown), so anyone can read exactly what it does.

### Want the details?

The [privacy page](https://quilldown.vercel.app/privacy) explains what is stored, where, and how to check it yourself.

Sharing

## Share a document without uploading it

Click Share and Quilldown compresses your document into the link itself. The part of a link after the # symbol is never sent to a server, so the document isn't stored anywhere. Whoever opens the link gets their own private copy in a new tab. You can also choose a preview-only link, so the person sees the finished page instead of the editor.

quilldown.vercel.app/#d=z.eJxLz…

### Two things to know

Long documents make long links, with a warning above about 8,000 characters and a hard stop at 64,000. And pasted images aren't included in shared links.

Appearance

## Comfortable to look at, day or night

### Light and dark themes

A calm theme for daytime and one for night. Your exports always stay light.

### Layouts that adapt

Resize the panes on a large screen, or use the single-pane view on a small one.

What Quilldown doesn't do

## The honest limits

No editor does everything. These are the things worth knowing before you rely on Quilldown.

- Your drafts live only in your browser. Clearing browser data deletes them and they can't be recovered, so export important documents as .md files.

- Browsers typically allow around 5 MB of local storage per site. Text uses very little, but pasted images count toward it.

- There's no real-time collaboration and no cloud sync between devices. Sharing works through links to a copy of the document.

- Word exports keep equations as TeX source and turn diagrams into images.

- PNG export isn't suited to very long documents.

- Saving straight back to a file on your computer works in Chrome and Edge only.

If something you need isn't here, [open an issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Dhruv-Dhameliya/quilldown/issues) and tell us what's missing.

Questions about the features

## Common questions

### Is Quilldown really free?

Yes. There's no account, no paid tier and nothing to sign up for. The code is open source under the MIT license.

### What can I export to?

PDF, Word (.docx), PNG, EPUB, HTML, Markdown and plain text. You can also copy the preview straight into Google Docs with Copy for Docs.

### Does Quilldown support math and diagrams?

Yes. Write LaTeX between dollar signs and it's typeset with KaTeX, and put Mermaid code in a mermaid code block to draw flowcharts, sequence diagrams and more. Both update live as you type.

### Can I work on more than one document at a time?

Yes. Each document opens in its own tab, and every tab is saved automatically in your browser as you type.

### Does it work offline?

Yes, after your first visit. The site is cached in your browser, so it loads, previews and exports without a connection.

### Is my writing uploaded anywhere?

No. Everything happens in your browser, including exports. Drafts are stored on your own device, which also means clearing your browser data deletes them, so export anything important as a .md file.

[See the full FAQ](https://quilldown.vercel.app/faq)

## See it for yourself

Open the editor and try any of this in a few seconds. No account, no setup, nothing to upload.

[Open the editor](https://quilldown.vercel.app/#editor)
[Browse the guides](https://quilldown.vercel.app/docs)

How it works

# How Quilldown works, from first word to finished file

Quilldown is a free online Markdown editor with a live preview. You write on one side, see the finished page on the other, then copy it or export it in the format you need. This page walks through each step and explains what happens to your writing along the way.

[Open the editor](https://quilldown.vercel.app/#editor)
[See the features](https://quilldown.vercel.app/features)

The short version

## Three steps, no setup

There's nothing to install and no account to make. Open the page and you're already in the editor.

- 1Write or pasteType, paste existing Markdown, drop in a file or start from a template.

- 2Watch it renderThe preview updates as you type.

- 3Copy or exportChoose the format at the end, when you know where the document is going.

1

## Step 1: Start with whatever you have

You can begin four ways, and all of them end up in the same editor.

- Type from scratch. Click into the editor and write. The toolbar has around 45 one-click snippets for headings, lists, tables, math and diagrams. If you know Markdown, you can ignore it and just type.

- Paste Markdown. Paste text you've already written, from a README, a notes app or an AI chat, and it renders right away.

- Open or drop a file. Use Open (Ctrl O) or drag .md, .markdown or .txt files onto the page. Several files at once are fine, and each opens in its own tab.

- Start from a template. Under New → Templates you'll find a README, meeting notes, résumé, blog post, email, tables, to-do list and general notes. Each opens in its own tab.

### Pictures work too

You can also paste a screenshot or drop in a picture. Quilldown resizes it, keeps it inside the document and includes it when you export.

### New to Markdown?

You only need a few symbols to get going.

# Big heading## Smaller one

Big headingSmaller one

A # and a space before a line makes it a heading. Use ## for a smaller one.

**bold** and *italic*

bold and italic

Put ** around words to make them bold, and * around words for italics.

- First idea- Second idea

- First idea
- Second idea

A - and a space at the start of a line makes a bullet.

[Quilldown](https://quilldown.vercel.app)

Quilldown

Text in square brackets followed by a web address in round brackets makes a link.

The [Markdown cheat sheet](https://quilldown.vercel.app/docs/markdown-cheat-sheet) shows every symbol with a live example.

untitled.md

```
# Weekly update

Ship **fast**, write _well_.
```

Step 1: write, paste or open

2

## Step 2: See the finished page as you write

The preview updates as you type. Headings become headings, lists become lists, and tables, task lists and code blocks show up as they'll look in the final document.

### What you'll see rendered

- GitHub-style Markdown, including tables, task lists and strikethrough

- Code with syntax highlighting

- LaTeX equations, drawn with KaTeX

- Diagrams, drawn from text with Mermaid

- Footnotes, numbered and linked both ways

- Callouts such as Note, Tip and Warning

- Two panes that move together. Scroll either side and the other follows, lined up block by block, so a long table won't leave the panes out of step.

- Change the view. Use split view, editor only or preview only, and drag the divider to resize. On a phone you see one pane at a time, and you switch with the buttons in the top bar.

- Your work is saved as you go. Every tab autosaves in your browser, so closing the page doesn't lose your draft.

untitled.md

```
# Weekly update

Ship **fast**, write _well_.

- Draft
- Review
```

Weekly updateShip fast, write well.

- Draft
- Review

Step 2: the preview follows every keystroke

3

## Step 3: Choose where it goes

You decide the format last. The same source can become any of these.

### Not sure which to pick?

Use Copy for Docs.Heading sizes Docs understands, and it takes on the font of your document. Prefer a file? Export a Word (.docx) document, which also opens in Google Docs.

Good to know: Word keeps equations as TeX source text, and diagrams become images.

Export to PDF.A print-ready document, and your equations look exactly as they do in the preview.

Good to know: choose "Save as PDF" in the print dialog, and turn on "Background graphics" if code blocks or tables look flat.

Copy HTML, or export an HTML page.Copy HTML gives you clean markup for a website or CMS. Export HTML gives you a standalone, styled web page.

Export to EPUB.An e-book for Apple Books, Kobo and other readers.

Click Share.Quilldown builds a link that contains your document. Whoever opens it gets their own private copy in a new tab. You can also choose a preview-only link.

Good to know: long documents make long links, and pasted images aren't included.

### If you're pasting into another app

- Copy formatted text to paste into an email, a note or another editor.

- Copy for Google Docs uses heading sizes Docs understands (H1 at 23 pt, H2 at 17 pt, H3 at 14 pt, body text at 12 pt) and sets no font, so it takes on the font of your document.

- Copy HTML gives you clean markup for a website or CMS.

- Copy Markdown gives you the source again.

### If you're saving a file

- PDF. Choose Export → PDF, then pick "Save as PDF" in the print dialog. Best when you want a print-ready document or your equations to look exactly as they do in the preview.

- Word (.docx). A real Word document that also opens in Google Docs and Pages.

- PNG. An image of the whole document, for quick sharing.

- EPUB. An e-book for Apple Books, Kobo and other readers.

- HTML. A standalone, styled web page.

- Markdown (.md) and plain text (.txt). The source with or without markup.

### If you're sending it to someone

Click Share and Quilldown builds a link that contains your document. Whoever opens it gets their own private copy in a new tab. You can also choose a preview-only link.

### Exports are always light

Exports always come out in a clean, light, print-friendly style, even if you write in dark mode.

Export

- PDFSave as PDF
- Word.docx
- Image.png
- E-book.epub
- Web page.html
- Markdown.md
- Plain text.txt

Step 3: pick the format you need

Try it in a minute

## Make your first document in about a minute

A quick walk-through you can follow in the editor.

### Your first minute

- Open the editor and click New → Templates → Meeting notes. A new tab opens with a starter document.

- Change the title. Replace the first line, and watch the preview change as you type.

- Add a task list. Type a dash, a space and [ ] before an item, then keep going. Each line becomes a checkbox in the preview.

- Add a table. Click Table, type in the grid or paste rows from a spreadsheet, and insert it.

- Export it. Choose Export → PDF and save it, or use Copy for Docs and paste into a Google Doc.

[Open the editor and try it](https://quilldown.vercel.app/#editor)

### Or try it right here

Change the text and the preview updates. Nothing you type leaves this page.

Markdown

[Open this in the full editor](https://quilldown.vercel.app/#editor)

Behind the scenes

## What happens to your writing

Quilldown is built so your document stays on your device. Here's what that means in practice.

Everything happens inside the box on the left.

### Rendering happens in your browser

The preview is produced on your own device as you type. Nothing is sent anywhere to draw it.

### Saving happens on your device

Drafts autosave to your browser's local storage. There is no account, so there is no cloud copy. Because of that, clearing your browser data also deletes your saved tabs, and they can't be recovered. Export anything important as a .md file, or press Ctrl S.

### Exports are made locally

PDF, Word, PNG, EPUB, HTML and the rest are created in your browser, and the files go straight to your device. Nothing is uploaded to produce them.

### Sharing puts the document in the link

When you click Share, your document is compressed and packed into the link itself. The part of a link after the # symbol isn't sent to a server, so the document isn't stored anywhere. Long documents make long links. There's a warning above about 8,000 characters and a hard stop at 64,000, and pasted images aren't included.

### Offline works after your first visit

Every library and font is bundled with the site, and a service worker caches it. After that, Quilldown loads and exports without a connection. In browsers that support it, you can install it as an app.

### You can check all of this

Open your browser's network panel while you write and you'll see nothing leaving. The code is also [public on GitHub](https://github.com/Dhruv-Dhameliya/quilldown). More in the [privacy details](https://quilldown.vercel.app/privacy).

Check it yourself
Press F12 and open the Network tab. Now write for a minute: you'll see no requests carrying your text.

Tips for good results

## Small things that make a difference

### Export to PDF when you have equations

Word keeps equations as TeX source text, and diagrams become images. PDF shows them exactly as in the preview.

### Flat code blocks or tables in a PDF?

Turn on "Background graphics" in the print options.

### Use PDF instead of PNG for long documents

A very long page is too tall for a single image.

### Use Chrome or Edge to save back to the original file

That's where Ctrl+S saves straight back to the file. In other browsers, Ctrl+S downloads a .md copy.

### Keep a backup of anything important

Export a .md file now and then, since drafts live only in your browser.

### Keep images modest

They're stored in your browser with the document, so many large images can reach the browser's storage limit (typically around 5 MB per site) before text ever would.

### Use Undo if you close a tab by accident

The message that appears has an Undo button.

Questions about how it works

## Common questions

### Do I need to install or sign up for anything?

No. Open the page and start writing. If you like, you can install it as an app in browsers that offer an Install button, but it isn't required.

### What happens to my document when I close the tab?

It's saved in your browser and will be there when you come back on the same device and browser.

### Can I move my drafts to another device?

There's no cloud sync, so drafts don't travel on their own. Export a .md file and open it on the other device, or use Share to send yourself a link.

### How can I be sure nothing is uploaded?

Open your browser's network panel and write for a minute. You'll see no requests carrying your text. The source code is also public on [GitHub](https://github.com/Dhruv-Dhameliya/quilldown).

### Can I use it without internet?

Yes, after your first visit. The site is cached, so it loads and exports offline.

[See the full FAQ](https://quilldown.vercel.app/faq)

Open the editor and write your first line. It takes a few seconds, and nothing leaves your browser.

Privacy

# Your writing stays on your device

Quilldown is a Markdown editor that runs entirely in your browser. What you write is never sent to a server, there's no account to create, and no cloud copy exists. This page explains what that means, what it doesn't cover, and how you can check it yourself.

[Open the editor](https://quilldown.vercel.app/#editor)
[View the source on GitHub](https://github.com/Dhruv-Dhameliya/quilldown)

At a glance

## The short version

Everything happens inside the box on the left.

### Nothing is uploaded

Typing, previewing, copying and exporting all happen on your device. Your text isn't sent anywhere.

### No account

There's no sign-up, no email address and no login, so there's nothing to link your writing to.

### Saved on your device only

Your drafts autosave in your browser so they're there when you return. That's the only copy.

### Open source

The code is public on [GitHub](https://github.com/Dhruv-Dhameliya/quilldown), so anyone can read what Quilldown does.

What's stored, and where

## What Quilldown keeps, and where it lives

Quilldown keeps two kinds of information, and both stay in your browser's storage on your own device.

### Your documents

Every open tab is autosaved to your browser's local storage as you type. Pasted images are stored with the document. These drafts exist only on your device. Nothing is copied to a server, so we can't see them, recover them or hand them to anyone.

### Your preferences

Quilldown remembers a few settings, such as your theme (light or dark) and whether you chose "Start in editor". These are stored the same way, in your browser, on your device.

### That's the full list

There's no profile, no history of what you've written and no record of which documents you've opened.

### How to remove it

To delete a draft, close its tab. To remove everything Quilldown has stored, including your preferences, clear this site's data in your browser settings. Once it's deleted, it's gone, because there's no other copy.

What Quilldown doesn't do

## What we don't do

### Kept on your device

- Your open tabs and drafts

- Images you pasted into a document

- Your theme, light or dark

- Your "Start in editor" choice

### Never happens

- We don't upload your text, at any point, for any reason.

- We don't ask you to make an account or give an email address.

- We don't measure or record what you write.

- We don't load third-party scripts, fonts or icons while you work. Everything the editor needs ships with the site.

- We don't send your documents to any AI service, converter or export server. Every export is created in your browser.

Exporting and converting

## Converting a document doesn't send it anywhere

Many online converters upload your file to their servers to process it. Quilldown doesn't. PDF, Word, PNG, EPUB, HTML, Markdown and plain text files are all generated inside your browser and saved straight to your device.

The PDF export uses your browser's own print dialog, so it works the same way: your document is turned into a file on your computer, not on ours.

Sharing

## How sharing works without storing your document

When you click Share, Quilldown compresses your document and packs it into the link itself. Nothing is uploaded and nothing is saved on a server.

This works because of how web addresses are built. The part of a link after the # symbol stays in the browser and isn't sent to the website's server when someone opens it. Whoever opens your link gets their own private copy in a new tab.

Sent to the serverquilldown.vercel.app/
Stays in the browser#d=z.eJxLz3Mo…

### What to know before you share

- Anyone who has the link can read the document. There's no password or expiry, because there's no account or server to enforce one.

- The link contains your content. If you paste it into a chat app, email or social post, that service can see the link, and so the document inside it.

- Pasted images aren't included in shared links.

- Long documents make long links. You'll see a warning above 8,000 characters and a hard stop at 64,000.

- Once you've sent a link, you can't take it back.

### If a document is sensitive

Don't share it as a link. Export it and send the file through a channel you trust.

Offline and third parties

## Built to work without the outside world

### Nothing loads from outside

Every library, font and icon Quilldown uses is bundled with the site. Nothing loads from third-party servers while you work, so there's no outside company that can see that you're using it.

### Cached after your first visit

A service worker caches the site on your device. From then on, Quilldown loads and exports without a connection. In browsers that support it, you can also install it as an app.

### Offline is a privacy option too

If you want to be sure, turn off your connection and keep writing. Everything still works.

Check it yourself

## Don't take our word for it

You can verify all of this in a couple of minutes.

- Open Quilldown and press F12 (or right-click and choose Inspect) to open your browser's developer tools.

- Go to the Network tab.

- Type a few lines in the editor, switch tabs, and try an export.

- Watch the list. You won't see requests carrying your text.

For a stronger test, load the page once, switch off your Wi-Fi and keep writing. Everything continues to work.

You can also read the source code on GitHub and see exactly how Quilldown stores, renders and exports your writing.

[View the source on GitHub](https://github.com/Dhruv-Dhameliya/quilldown)

### What the Network tab shows while you write

An illustration: type below and watch the list.

Type something private

Networkillustration

NameStatusType

No requests while you type

Characters typed: 0Requests carrying your text: 0

What this doesn't protect against

## The honest limits

"Nothing is uploaded" is a strong promise, but it isn't the same as "nothing can go wrong". These are the things worth knowing.

- Other people using your browser. Drafts are stored in your browser profile. If someone else uses your device and your browser profile, they can open Quilldown and see them. On a shared or public computer, clear the site's data when you finish, or use a private window.

- Browser extensions. Extensions you've installed can sometimes read the pages you visit. If you write sensitive material, check which extensions you trust.

- Clearing browser data. Deleting your browser data deletes your drafts. Nothing is stored elsewhere, so they can't be recovered. Export important documents as .md files.

- Shared links. As explained above, a link is your document. Treat it like the document itself.

- Copying and pasting. When you copy text and paste it into another app, that app's privacy rules apply from then on.

- Images linked from the web. If you add an image by its web address, your browser fetches it from that address, as it would on any web page. Images you paste or upload stay inside the document.

- Your device and network. Quilldown can't protect a device that's been compromised. It also doesn't change what your internet provider or workplace network can see about which sites you visit.

- The hosting of the website itself. Quilldown is served as static files by a hosting provider (Vercel). Like any website host, it receives the standard details of a page request, such as your IP address and which page you loaded, and it may keep ordinary server logs. Those requests never contain your writing.

Cookies and analytics

## Cookies, trackers and analytics

Quilldown doesn't use cookies or trackers on your writing, and nothing about what you write is measured or sent anywhere. The only things it keeps are your own drafts and a few preferences, all in your browser's storage on your device.

Quilldown doesn't run analytics on its pages.

Open source

## Open source, so it can be checked

Quilldown's code is public. That means developers can read how it works, security-minded people can check the claims on this page, and anyone can report a problem.

[Source code on GitHub](https://github.com/Dhruv-Dhameliya/quilldown)
[Report an issue](https://github.com/Dhruv-Dhameliya/quilldown/issues)

Tips

## Simple ways to keep your documents private

### Keep a backup

Export a .md backup of anything important, and store it somewhere you control.

### Shared computers

On a shared computer, use a private window or clear the site's data afterward.

### Sensitive documents

Share sensitive documents as files, not links.

### Want to be certain?

Load Quilldown once and then work offline.

### Update your browser

Keep your browser up to date, since browser security matters as much as the editor's.

Privacy questions

## Privacy questions

### Can you see what I write?

No. Your text stays in your browser and is never sent to us, so we can't see it.

### Do you store my documents on a server?

No. Drafts are saved in your browser's storage on your device. There's no server copy and no account.

### Can you recover a document I lost?

No. Because nothing is stored on our side, there's nothing to recover. That's the trade-off for real privacy, so export important documents as .md files.

### Is a shared link private?

The document isn't stored on a server, but anyone with the link can read it, and any app you paste the link into can see it. For sensitive documents, send a file instead.

### Does Quilldown use cookies?

It doesn't use cookies on your writing. It keeps your drafts and a few preferences, like your theme, in your browser's storage on your device.

### Does exporting to PDF or Word upload my document?

No. Every export is created in your browser and saved straight to your device.

### Can I use it offline to be extra sure?

Yes. After your first visit, Quilldown works without a connection.

### How do I delete everything?

Close your tabs, or clear this site's data in your browser settings to remove all drafts and preferences.

[See the full FAQ](https://quilldown.vercel.app/faq)

FAQ

# Frequently asked questions about Quilldown

Straight answers about how Quilldown works, what happens to your writing, how to export it, and what to do when something looks off. Can't find your question? Ask on GitHub and it may be added here.

8 questions

## Getting started

### What is Quilldown, and who is it for?

Quilldown is a free online Markdown editor that runs in your browser. You type Markdown on one side, a live preview updates on the other, and you copy or export the result as a PDF, Word file, PNG, EPUB, HTML page or plain text. It suits developers writing READMEs, students taking notes with equations, bloggers drafting posts, and anyone who prefers plain text.

### Is Quilldown free? Do I need an account?

Yes, it's free, and there's no account, sign-up or email address. Open the page and start writing.

### How do I start writing?

Open Quilldown and type in the editor. You can also paste existing Markdown, drop in a .md file, or start from one of eight templates under New → Templates. There's nothing to install or set up.

### Which browsers does Quilldown work in?

Any current version of Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari. A few extras, like linking a tab to a file on your computer and the Install button, need a Chromium-based browser such as Chrome or Edge.

### Does Quilldown work on phones and tablets?

Yes. On a small screen the editor shows one pane at a time, and you switch between writing and preview with the buttons in the top bar. You can also install it as an app in browsers that offer that.

### How is Quilldown different from Word or Google Docs?

The source is plain text, so your writing is portable, easy to search and works with Git. Formatting is typed (# for a heading, ** for bold) instead of clicked. You still end up with a finished document, because you can export a real Word file or paste into Google Docs.

### How is Quilldown different from other online Markdown editors?

The main differences are that it needs no account, keeps your text in your browser, works offline after your first visit, and exports to seven formats. It's a browser tool, so it doesn't manage folders of notes the way a desktop notes app can. If you need real-time collaboration or cloud sync, another tool is a better fit.

### Is Quilldown open source?

Yes. The code is public on [GitHub](https://github.com/Dhruv-Dhameliya/quilldown) under the MIT License, so you can read it, use it, change it and share it.

11 questions

## Privacy and storage

### Is Quilldown private? Where is my text stored?

Your text stays in your browser. Each tab autosaves to your device's local storage, and nothing you write is uploaded to a server. There's no account, so there's no cloud copy either. The [privacy page](https://quilldown.vercel.app/privacy) explains it in full.

### Can anyone else see what I write?

No. Because your documents never reach a server, neither the maintainer nor anyone else can see or recover them. The exception is a shared link, which contains the document itself, so anyone with the link can read it.

### Does Quilldown use cookies, trackers or analytics?

No analytics, no trackers and no third-party requests while you work. It stores your drafts and a few preferences, such as your theme, in your browser on your device.

### How can I check that nothing is uploaded?

Open your browser's developer tools (F12), go to the Network tab, and type in the editor. You won't see requests carrying your text. For a stronger test, load the page once, switch off your connection and keep writing. The code is also public on [GitHub](https://github.com/Dhruv-Dhameliya/quilldown).

### What happens if I clear my browser data?

Saved tabs are removed and can't be recovered, because nothing is stored anywhere else. Export important documents with Export → Markdown (.md) or Ctrl+S first.

### Are my drafts kept in a private or incognito window?

Browsers usually discard a site's stored data when you close a private window, so treat drafts there as temporary and export anything you want to keep.

### How do I back up my documents?

Use Export → Markdown (.md) or press Ctrl+S to save a .md file. In Chrome and Edge, a tab linked to a file saves straight back to that file, which is the easiest backup.

### How do I delete everything Quilldown has stored?

Close your tabs to remove those documents, or clear this site's data in your browser settings to remove all drafts and preferences. Once cleared, they're gone.

### Is it safe to paste Markdown or HTML from an unknown source?

The preview is sanitized before it's shown, so scripts hidden in pasted content shouldn't run. As with anything you paste, use judgment with material you don't trust.

### Who owns what I write in Quilldown?

You do. Quilldown doesn't receive your writing, and the MIT License applies to the editor's code, not to your documents.

### Is Quilldown suitable for confidential or work documents?

Your text isn't sent to any server, which suits sensitive drafting. Keep in mind the limits: other people using your browser profile can open your drafts, and shared links contain the document. See the [privacy page](https://quilldown.vercel.app/privacy) for the full list.

14 questions

## Markdown basics

### What is Markdown?

Markdown is a way of formatting plain text using simple symbols. A # makes a heading, ** makes bold text and a dash makes a bullet. The file stays plain text, so any editor can open it. See [What is Markdown?](https://quilldown.vercel.app/docs/what-is-markdown) for a full introduction.

### What is a .md file, and how do I open one?

A .md file is a plain-text file written in Markdown. To open one in Quilldown, click Open (Ctrl+O) or drag the file onto the page. It also opens in any text editor, but there you see the raw symbols instead of the formatted page.

### Which Markdown flavor does Quilldown support?

GitHub Flavored Markdown: tables, task lists, strikethrough, autolinks and fenced code blocks with syntax highlighting. On top of that you get KaTeX math, Mermaid diagrams, footnotes, emoji shortcodes and GitHub-style callouts.

### How do I make a heading, bold text, italics, a list or a link?

Start a line with # and a space for a heading (## for a smaller one). Wrap words in ** for bold and * for italics. Start a line with - and a space for a bullet. Write a link as [text](https://example.com). The [Markdown cheat sheet](https://quilldown.vercel.app/docs/markdown-cheat-sheet) shows every symbol with a live example.

```
# A heading

Some **bold** and *italic* words.

- A bullet
- Another bullet

[A link](https://commonmark.org)
```

### How do I make a new paragraph or a line break?

Leave a blank line between paragraphs. To break a line inside a paragraph, end the line with two spaces or a backslash.

### How do I add a code block with syntax highlighting?

Put your code between two lines of three backticks and add the language name after the first set, for example js or python. Quilldown highlights dozens of languages and adds a one-click copy button in the preview.

```
```js
const answer = 42;
console.log(answer);
```
```

### How do I make a task list?

Start each line with a dash, a space and [ ] for an unchecked box or [x] for a checked one. They render as checkboxes in the preview.

```
- [x] Write the draft
- [ ] Review it
- [ ] Publish
```

### How do I make a table without typing pipes?

Click Table to build one in a visual grid, set each column's alignment and insert it. You can also paste rows from Excel or Google Sheets. See [Markdown tables](https://quilldown.vercel.app/docs/markdown-table-generator).

```
| Plan   | Price |
| :----- | ----: |
| Editor | Free  |
| Export | Free  |
```

### How do I add images?

Paste a screenshot, drop a picture onto the editor, or use Image → Upload. Images are resized, stored with the document and included in every export.

### How do I add footnotes?

Write [^1] where the note belongs and [^1]: your note text on its own line. Quilldown numbers them, collects them at the bottom and links both ways. In a Word export they become real footnotes.

```
A claim that needs a source.[^1]

[^1]: Here is the source.
```

### How do I add callouts like Note or Warning?

Use the Callouts dropdown, or start a quote with > [!NOTE], [!TIP], [!IMPORTANT], [!WARNING] or [!CAUTION]. They render as GitHub-style boxes.

```
> [!NOTE]
> Useful information that people should know.

> [!WARNING]
> Urgent information that needs attention.
```

### Can I use underline, highlight or centered text?

Yes, through the toolbar or inline HTML. Quilldown supports tags such as u, mark, kbd, sub, sup and details, plus alignment on blocks, so you can also make collapsible sections and centered blocks.

### Does Quilldown support emoji?

Yes. Use the emoji picker (search by name, choose a skin tone) or type a colon and a few letters, like :roc, to pick from suggestions. A finished :tada: becomes 🎉. See [Emoji shortcodes](https://quilldown.vercel.app/docs/emoji-in-markdown).

### Are there templates?

Yes, eight: README, meeting notes, résumé, blog post, email, tables, to-do list and notes. Each opens in its own tab under New → Templates.

4 questions

## Math and diagrams

### Does Quilldown support LaTeX math?

Yes. Write inline math between single dollar signs and display math between double dollar signs. It renders with KaTeX, including fractions, sums, integrals, matrices and aligned equations. See [Math in Markdown](https://quilldown.vercel.app/docs/math-in-markdown).

```
Euler's identity, $e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0$, links five constants.

$$
x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}
$$
```

### What kinds of diagrams can I draw?

Eight types from plain text using Mermaid: flowchart, sequence, class, state, ER, Gantt, pie and mind map. Each has a ready-made template on the toolbar. See [Diagrams in Markdown](https://quilldown.vercel.app/docs/diagrams-in-markdown).

```
```mermaid
flowchart LR
A[Write] --> B{Looks right?}
B -- Yes --> C[Export]
B -- No --> A
```
```

### Do math and diagrams work in dark mode?

Yes, diagrams follow your light or dark theme. Exports always come out in a clean, light, print-friendly style.

### Why do equations and diagrams look different in Word?

Word has no KaTeX or Mermaid renderer, so the .docx keeps equations as their TeX source and inserts diagrams as images. If your equations need to look typeset, export to PDF, where they appear exactly as in the preview.

7 questions

## Writing tools

### What keyboard shortcuts does Quilldown have?

On a Mac, use ⌘ instead of Ctrl. The tab shortcuts work in the full-screen editor.

- BoldCtrlB
- ItalicCtrlI
- UnderlineCtrlU
- StrikethroughCtrlShiftX
- Inline codeCtrlE
- LinkCtrlK
- FindCtrlF
- ReplaceCtrlH
- SaveCtrlS
- OpenCtrlO
- New tabCtrlAltN
- Close tabCtrlAltW
- Next or previous tabCtrlAlt←→
- Leave full screenEsc

### Does Enter continue a list?

Yes. Enter continues a list and ends it on an empty item, and Tab and Shift+Tab indent and outdent. Applying a formatting snippet twice removes it.

### Can I find and replace with regular expressions?

Yes. Press Ctrl+F or Ctrl+H, then turn on match case, whole word or regex. Regex replacements support $1 groups, and Replace all is a single undo step.

### What is the outline sidebar?

A clickable list of all your headings, opened from the list icon in the top bar. The current section follows your scroll, so you can jump around long documents.

### How does the toolbar work?

It has 45+ one-click snippets grouped into text styles, structure, inserts, math, diagrams, callouts and layout. Hover any button to see its shortcut.

### Can I change the layout?

Yes. Choose editor only, split or preview only, and drag the divider to resize. Scrolling is synced block by block, so both sides stay aligned.

### Is there a dark mode?

Yes, a light and a dark theme. Exports are always light.

7 questions

## Files and offline

### Can I have several documents open at once?

Yes, up to 30 tabs. Add one with +, drag to reorder, double-click to rename and middle-click to close. Closed one by accident? Press Undo in the message that appears.

### Which files can I open?

.md, .markdown, .mdown, .mkd, .txt and .text files, up to 5 MB each. Open several at once or drag them onto the page, and each lands in its own tab.

### Can I save back to the original file?

In Chrome and Edge, a tab you open stays linked to its file. A dot on the tab shows the link (orange means unsaved changes), and Ctrl+S saves straight back. In other browsers, Ctrl+S downloads a .md copy instead.

### Does Quilldown work offline?

Yes. Everything ships with the site, and after your first visit a service worker caches it, so it loads and exports without a connection.

### Can I install Quilldown as an app?

Yes, in Chrome, Edge and other browsers that support it, using the Install button. Once installed, it also appears in your system's "Open with" menu for Markdown files.

### Can I move my documents to another device?

There's no cloud sync, so drafts don't travel on their own. Export a .md file and open it on the other device, or use Share to send yourself a link.

### Can I host Quilldown myself?

Quilldown is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no build step, and the MIT License allows it, so you can copy the files to any static host. Offline use and the Install button need the site to be served over HTTPS. Keep the copyright notice and the licenses of the bundled libraries.

4 questions

## Copying

### What can I copy?

Formatted text as it looks in the preview, Markdown, clean HTML, or a version made for Google Docs. Copy buttons sit on each pane, and Copy HTML is in the top-bar Copy menu.

### What is Copy for Docs?

A copy that pastes with point sizes Google Docs and Word understand: H1 at 23 pt, H2 at 17 pt, H3 at 14 pt and body text at 12 pt. It sets no font, so pasted text takes on the font of your document.

### How do I copy clean HTML for a website or CMS?

Use Copy → HTML from the top bar. It puts clean markup on your clipboard. See [Markdown to HTML](https://quilldown.vercel.app/docs/markdown-to-html).

### Does copied Markdown include my images?

Yes. Copying or saving Markdown embeds your images, so the text is self-contained, though it becomes longer.

12 questions

## Exporting

### Which formats can I export to?

PDF, Word (.docx), PNG, EPUB, HTML, Markdown (.md) and plain text (.txt). Each is created in your browser and saved straight to your device.

Format |
Best for |
One thing to know |

PDF |
Print-ready files and equations |
Made through your browser's print dialog |

Word (.docx) |
Editing in Word, Docs or Pages |
Equations stay as TeX, diagrams become images |

PNG |
Quick sharing as one image |
Too tall for very long documents |

EPUB |
Reading on an e-reader |
Each top-level heading becomes a chapter |

HTML |
A standalone web page |
Copy HTML gives clean markup instead |

Markdown, text |
Your plain source |
No formatting in the text file |

### How do I convert Markdown to PDF?

Write or paste your Markdown, choose Export → PDF, and pick "Save as PDF" as the destination in the print dialog. It's free, private and works offline, and the text stays selectable. See [Markdown to PDF](https://quilldown.vercel.app/docs/markdown-to-pdf).

### Can I set the page size, margins or page numbers in the PDF?

The print dialog controls paper size, margins and headers or footers, since the PDF is made through your browser. The [Markdown to PDF](https://quilldown.vercel.app/docs/markdown-to-pdf) guide covers page breaks and print settings.

### Why does my PDF look flat, or lose code block colors?

Turn on "Background graphics" in the print options, and the shaded code blocks and tables come back.

### How do I convert Markdown to Word?

Choose Export → Word (.docx). You get a real Word document with heading styles, lists, tables, links, code, callouts, images, diagrams and footnotes. It also opens in Google Docs and Pages. See [Markdown to Word](https://quilldown.vercel.app/docs/markdown-to-word).

### How do I convert Markdown to Google Docs?

There are two ways. Click Copy for Docs on the preview and paste into a Google Doc, or export a .docx and open it in Docs.

### How do I convert Markdown to HTML?

Use Copy → HTML for clean markup or Export → HTML for a standalone, styled web page.

### How do I make an EPUB e-book from Markdown?

Choose Export → EPUB. Each top-level heading becomes a chapter, with a table of contents, and the file works in Apple Books, Kobo and other readers.

### Can I export my document as an image?

Yes, Export → PNG gives you one picture of the whole document. Very long documents are too tall for a single PNG, so use PDF for those.

### Can I paste Markdown from an AI chat and turn it into a document?

Yes. Paste it into the editor and it renders straight away, including tables and code. Then copy it into Google Docs or export it as PDF or Word. See [Markdown to Word](https://quilldown.vercel.app/docs/markdown-to-word).

### Why do exports always look light, even in dark mode?

So they print and read well anywhere. The editor theme only affects what you see while you write.

### Does exporting upload my document?

No. Every export is generated in your browser, so nothing is sent to a converter or server.

4 questions

## Sharing

### How does sharing work?

Click Share and Quilldown packs your document into the link itself. Nothing is uploaded, and whoever opens the link gets their own copy in a new tab.

### Is a shared link private?

The document isn't stored on a server, but anyone with the link can read it, and any app you paste the link into can see it. For sensitive documents, send a file instead.

### Is there a size limit for shared links?

You'll see a warning above about 8,000 characters, and links over 64,000 characters are refused. Pasted images aren't included.

### Can I share a preview-only link?

Yes. Choose "Open in preview-only mode" and the person sees the finished page instead of the editor.

8 questions

## Troubleshooting

### My drafts disappeared. What happened?

The usual causes are cleared browser data, a private window, or a different browser or device, since drafts live only in the browser where you wrote them. If you closed a tab, press Undo right away. Export .md backups to avoid this next time.

### Ctrl+S downloads a file instead of saving to my original file. Why?

Saving back to a linked file works in Chrome and Edge only, and the tab must have been opened from a file. In other browsers, Ctrl+S downloads a .md copy.

### I can't find the Install button.

It appears only in browsers that support installing web apps, such as Chrome and Edge. If you've already installed Quilldown, you won't see it again.

### The editor warned me about storage. What should I do?

Browsers allow roughly 5 MB of local storage per site, and pasted images count toward it. If the status bar says "Not saved (storage full)", export the document, then shrink or remove large images.

### Undo stopped working after I switched tabs.

Switching tabs clears the editor's undo history for that tab. Finish an edit before you switch.

### My table or diagram doesn't render.

Check the syntax: tables need a header row with dashes under it, and diagrams need a code block starting with mermaid. The Table button and the diagram templates give you a correct starting point.

### My shared link won't open or is too long.

Very long documents make very long links, and above 64,000 characters the link is refused. Export the document as a file instead.

### How do I report a bug?

Open an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/Dhruv-Dhameliya/quilldown/issues) with your browser and, if you can, a small sample of the Markdown involved. Share only text you're comfortable making public.

Quilldown is built and maintained by one developer. See the [About](https://quilldown.vercel.app/about) page.

### Can I use Quilldown for work or commercially?

Yes. The editor is free to use for any purpose, and the code is released under the MIT License.

### How can I suggest a feature or a new FAQ?

Open an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/Dhruv-Dhameliya/quilldown/issues). Good FAQ suggestions come from real questions, so tell us what you were trying to do.

About

# About Quilldown

Quilldown is a free Markdown editor that runs entirely in your browser. This page explains what it is, why it exists, and how to reach the person who builds it.

[Open the editor](https://quilldown.vercel.app/#editor)
[View source on GitHub](https://github.com/Dhruv-Dhameliya/quilldown)

### On this page

## What Quilldown is

Quilldown is a Markdown editor for people who like to write in plain text but need a polished result. You type Markdown on one side and the formatted document appears on the other as you go. It supports GitHub Flavored Markdown, LaTeX math and Mermaid diagrams. When you're finished, you can copy the result or export it as a PDF, a Word document, a PNG image, an EPUB e-book, an HTML page, Markdown or plain text.

It's a single web page. There's nothing to sign up for, nothing to install, and no server that receives your writing.

## Why it exists

Most Markdown tools fall into one of two groups: heavyweight note-taking apps that want you to live inside them, or bare-bones previewers that stop at showing you the result. Quilldown aims for the space between. It should open instantly, stay out of your way, and make the last step painless, whether that means a PDF for submission, a Word file for a colleague, a web page for a blog, or a paste into another app.

I built it because every Markdown editor I tried felt the same: generic, short on features, and unable to copy the formatted text the way it looks in the preview. So I made the one I wanted. You're welcome.1

## Five ideas behind every decision

-   Private by default. What you write isn't sent anywhere, and there's no account to tie it to. Drafts are saved in your own browser, and every library and font is bundled with the site, so the editor makes no third-party requests while you write. [Read more](https://quilldown.vercel.app/privacy)

-   Calm and fast. A quiet interface and a live preview that keeps up with your typing. Scrolling is synced block by block, so you never lose your place. [Read more](https://quilldown.vercel.app/features)

-   Useful output. What matters is what comes out the other end. Quilldown exports to seven formats and offers several ways to copy, including a version made for Google Docs with real heading sizes (H1 at 23 pt, H2 at 17 pt, H3 at 14 pt, body at 12 pt) that sets no font, so your text takes on the font of the document you paste it into. [Read more](https://quilldown.vercel.app/features#copy-export)

-   Honest about limits. There's no real-time collaboration and no cloud sync, and drafts live only in your browser. This site says so plainly instead of hiding it. [Read more](https://quilldown.vercel.app/features#limits)

-   Open to inspection. Quilldown is written in plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no build step, and the code is public on GitHub under the MIT License. You can read exactly how it works. [Read more](https://github.com/Dhruv-Dhameliya/quilldown)

Want the details? See [how Quilldown works](https://quilldown.vercel.app/how-quilldown-works), the [full feature list](https://quilldown.vercel.app/features) and the [privacy page](https://quilldown.vercel.app/privacy).

## What Quilldown isn't

## Built on other people's open-source work

Quilldown's own code is released under the MIT License, which means you're free to use, copy, modify and share it, as long as you keep the copyright notice.

It also stands on the shoulders of other open-source projects, all bundled with the site so nothing loads from a third-party server. Each of these keeps its own license.

- [marked](https://marked.js.org)

- [DOMPurify](https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify)

- [highlight.js](https://highlightjs.org)

- [KaTeX](https://katex.org)

- [Mermaid](https://mermaid.js.org)

- [docx](https://docx.js.org)

- [html2canvas](https://html2canvas.hertzen.com)

- [Emojibase](https://emojibase.dev)

- [Nunito](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Nunito)

- [Fraunces](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Fraunces)

- [JetBrains Mono](https://www.jetbrains.com/lp/mono/)

[Read the license](https://github.com/Dhruv-Dhameliya/quilldown/blob/main/LICENSE) · [Browse the source](https://github.com/Dhruv-Dhameliya/quilldown) · [Report an issue](https://github.com/Dhruv-Dhameliya/quilldown/issues)

## Who makes it

1 Quilldown is built and maintained by Dhruv Dhameliya. It's open source, and bug reports and suggestions are welcome on GitHub. [GitHub profile](https://github.com/Dhruv-Dhameliya)

## Contact and feedback

The best way to reach the maintainer is through GitHub.

- Bug reports and feature requests. Open an issue on the [Quilldown repository](https://github.com/Dhruv-Dhameliya/quilldown/issues). Include your browser and, if you can, a small sample of the Markdown involved.

- General, partnership and media enquiries. Visit the [maintainer's GitHub profile](https://github.com/Dhruv-Dhameliya) and follow the contact links there.

- Source code. Browse or fork the [Quilldown repository](https://github.com/Dhruv-Dhameliya/quilldown).

## Frequently asked questions

### Is Quilldown really free?

Yes. There's no account, no sign-up and no email address to give. And no ads.

### Does Quilldown collect or store my documents?

No. What you write stays in your browser, and drafts are autosaved to your own device only. Nothing is uploaded, there's no server copy, and there's no analytics. The [privacy page](https://quilldown.vercel.app/privacy) lists exactly what is stored.

### Is Quilldown open source?

Yes. The code is public on [GitHub](https://github.com/Dhruv-Dhameliya/quilldown) under the MIT License, so you can read it, use it, change it and share it.

### Who makes Quilldown?

See the Who makes it section above.

### How do I report a bug or suggest a feature?

Open an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/Dhruv-Dhameliya/quilldown/issues) with your browser and, if possible, a small sample of the Markdown involved.

### How can I contact the maintainer for press or partnership questions?

Use the contact links on the maintainer's [GitHub profile](https://github.com/Dhruv-Dhameliya).
